findings.observed: Cleared by route (a). B-05 now names, per case, in-repo material for both halves of prd.md D2's criterion, and each half checks out in this worktree: `.kiro/specs/afk-v2-acceptance-scope-gates/slices/02-behavior-coverage-gate/contract-review.json` and `05-test-cost-split-and-caching/contract-review.json` both carry `"verdict": "ACCEPT"`, and `03-candidate-evaluator-isolation/qa-review.json` and `08-file-scope-gate/qa-review.json` both carry `"verdict": "PASS"` with `"failureClass": "NONE"`. The prompt-reconstruction inputs the contract names (each slice's committed `contract.md`, `acceptance-manifest.json` and `qa-report-r*-a1.md`) are all present in those directories. The human confirmation is a reachable commit: `dbd6fdc266ce48253a81e051bf724c4d9a92e664` is the merge of PR #256 (2026-09-12) and `git merge-base --is-ancestor dbd6fdc HEAD` exits 0 on this branch. The contract records the consequence honestly rather than papering over it — only final-round verdicts are used, because a round-1 `REVISE` would need the round-1 contract pair, which no commit carries. B-06's source-name list and fallback clause were restated to match and now explicitly bar citing the absent `.afk/artifacts/**/reviews/` tree as the origin of an `expected` value, which closes the reviewer's inability to tell a reconstruction from an invention. findings.evidence: "the `05-` `evaluator-qa` case reads `FAIL` / `IMPLEMENTATION`; the `04-`, `06-` and `07-` `evaluator-contract` cases each read `ACCEPT`; and the `08-` and `09-` `evaluator-qa` cases each read `PASS` / `NONE`."
findings.expected: A seed pack whose purpose is to score candidate evaluators should let a role's cases discriminate — for a role with more than one case, at least one case whose expectation a degenerate always-same-answer evaluator would get wrong, or a recorded decision that this pack's sources cannot supply one and where the counter-case will come from.
findings.observed: After the revision every `evaluator-contract` case in the pack expects `ACCEPT` (`04-`, `06-`, `07-`) and both `evaluator-qa` PRD 4 cases expect `PASS`/`NONE`, so a candidate that answers `ACCEPT` to every contract prompt scores 3/3 on that role, and the two PRD 4 QA cases add no signal a stuck-at-`PASS` candidate would fail. The prior text left `06-`/`07-` open ("a `verdict` in `ACCEPT`/`REVISE`"), so this uniformity is revision-caused. B-05 does record why: only final-round verdicts are reachable, and a round-1 `REVISE` would need the uncommitted round-1 contract pair. That recorded reason is sound and evidence-backed, and `05-`'s `FAIL`/`IMPLEMENTATION` and `04-`'s false-premise `ACCEPT` still carry real discrimination, so this is advisory: the pack is honest about its own limits, but a reader should not read a high score on the contract role as evidence of evaluator quality.
findings.clearCondition: B-05 or the non-goals note in one sentence that the pack contains no `REVISE` contract expectation and no `FAIL` QA expectation drawn from PRD 4, so a per-role score on those cases cannot separate a correct evaluator from a stuck-at-`ACCEPT`/`PASS` one, and name the later source (or slice) that would supply the counter-case; alternatively the README requirement in B-07 carries that caveat alongside the per-case table.
